gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the yearly electricity cost of leaving the target running at a relative's house, or how many months the box takes to pay for itself against cloud backup. Worked out from spec-sheet or reviewer wattage and the August 2026 EIA residential rate (18.16¢/kWh), the cheapest box to buy is also the cheapest to run: a DS124 costs about $5.47 a year with its drive asleep and pays back its $159.99 price against Backblaze B2 in about 6 months at 4 TB. A UGREEN DH2300 costs about $15.91 a year at its measured idle and takes about 9 months.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited: Synology's Hyper Backup tech-spec page (destinations and a 65,535-version limit, but no power, price or cost-per-TB figures) and the KB 'Destination' help page (it rendered empty, with no figures). ChatGPT's own answer gives purchase prices only ($159.99 DS124, $214.99 DS223j) and never mentions running cost or a comparison with cloud. I did not open the uncited OutletPicks 'cost per drive bay' page, which may cover part of a per-dollar comparison but not power or payback.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's DS124 pick on total cost as well as sticker price. It is the cheapest to buy and to run: about $176 over 3 years for the box plus power, against about $189 for the TerraMaster F2-212, $229 for the DS223j and $288 for the UGREEN DH2300, all with drive asleep except the DH2300. At 4 TB stored, every NAS box pays itself back against B2 within a year, so cloud only wins for very small backups (around 2 TB-years or less for the DS124). This favors the Synology Vault pick over the UGREEN rows in our current page on cost as well as features.
